I am an old woman, 71 years, farming this small rented piece of land here in the South East. My back is not what it used to be, but I still go to the farm. This cassava and cocoyam plot is small, not even one-third of a hectare, and since it is rented land I do not want to spend too much money on it — the owner can take it back any season. I mix my cassava with cocoyam and some melon like my mother taught me, and I depend on the small money my children send me from the city.

I will not buy fertilizer bag this year — cassava grows well enough in our soil without it, and one bag is too much money for this small plot on land that is not mine. I put the goat droppings and the kitchen ash I gather near the house on the plot, that one costs me nothing. For the cassava stems, I use the ones I kept from last year's harvest, same as my neighbors — those improved TMS stems the agro people talk about, I have not seen them and they cost money. No spraying, no pumping water — rain is what we have. I do most of the weeding myself, slowly, and when the weeds grow too much before harvest I will call one of my grandchildren or pay a young boy small money for one or two days.
